Indicator: Persons below 150% of the federal poverty level
Adults aged ≥25 years without a high-school diploma

Principal component analysis of the correlation matrix of six county indicators (n = 3,134 counties with all six). Indicators were standardized to z-scores before extraction; median household income was sign-reversed so that every indicator increases with deprivation. Loadings are indicator-component correlations (coefficient × √eigenvalue); coefficients are eigenvector elements.

The EDI is the PC1 score, converted to national percentiles (0-100). PC1 from this full decomposition reproduces the stored raw EDI score (Pearson r = 1.000000); against the EDI percentiles its ranking is identical (Spearman ρ = 1.000), and the Pearson correlation is 0.962 because the percentile conversion is nonlinear. Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin measure 0.81; Bartlett test of sphericity χ² = 11,256, df = 15, P < 0.001.

Two components have eigenvalues above 1. PC2 (eigenvalue 1.03) is dominated by housing cost burden and does not exceed the 95th percentile of eigenvalues from 1,000 permuted datasets (1.05); parallel analysis retains one component, and the index retains PC1 only, as a single economic deprivation dimension. Software: Python 3.11, scikit-learn 1.4 (PCA, full singular value decomposition; StandardScaler).

PC2 sign is fixed so that its coefficients sum to a positive value; PC2 orientation is otherwise arbitrary. CCT = cardiac computed tomography; CI = confidence interval; CMR = cardiac magnetic resonance; EDI = economic deprivation index; IRR = incidence rate ratio; NB2 = negative binomial (quadratic variance); NE = not estimable; RUCC = Rural-Urban Continuum Code; SDI = Social Deprivation Index; SVI = Social Vulnerability Index.
